attempts_read.what_it_did: Attempt 1 reconstructed the entire multi-layer container format from scratch (211 agent messages, 188 tool calls, ~108 min). It found that zrq is a stripped amd64 PIE relying on obsolete glibc malloc/free hooks, so it segfaults on the worker's modern libc; it therefore built an Ubuntu 18.04 Docker fixture and used known-good encodings of its own sample inputs as an oracle throughout. Working outward from the damaged artifact: quiz.zrq is 89,124 bytes = 4,244 records of 21 bytes with a 21,548-byte zero suffix after offset 67,575. It established that the writer weaves a flat buffer with wire[k*N+r] = flat[21*r + ((5*k) mod 21)] (an index permutation by 5 mod 21), and that after undoing the weave each codeword is 15 systematic symbols plus 6 Reed-Solomon/GF(256) parity symbols over polynomial 0x11d, with the coefficient matrix at 0x20b660 and exp/log tables at 0x20b060/0x20b260. It solved small overdetermined Gaussian systems in GF(256) to recover the erased suffix, yielding 63,660 pre-FEC bytes (11 trailing 0xff pad). Note it initially got the layout wrong twice (simple stripe hypothesis, then a 'globally transposed 21 symbol planes' model) and corrected each via runtime index/buffer traces. Next layer: a Huffman container whose header is 255 merge pairs (right_representative, left_representative) plus a repeated final representative; because codes were emitted walking leaf-to-root, decoding requires reversing the whole meaningful bitstream and then reversing the decoded symbol sequence, with the 8 possible zero-bit paddings enumerated because the format stores no pad count. Beneath that: 35,611 fixed-width LZW tokens that are NOT in logical order — they were stored in heap nodes and emitted in the allocator VM's linked-list traversal order. The small-fixture permutation failed to extrapolate once glibc crossed its large-bin layout, so it built an exact-size oracle: generate a large input in Ubuntu 18.04 that encodes to exactly 35,611 codes, align emitted order against known LZW codes, and read off the permutation (two independent inputs agreed; packed mapping SHA-256 74bc7a6348024964...(truncated)), embedded in the solver as 412 Base85 chars of uint16 deltas. Applying the inverse permutation, standard LZW decode, and the format's final byte reversal gave a 90,989-byte directory image (SHA-256 4704e1a350205026...(truncated)). Final step: it parsed that image as a serialized filesystem traversal of records 'token NUL uint64_le(size) data', where slash components are queued SIBLING directories rather than parents, and replayed the traversal as a FIFO queue (collections.deque, popleft) using Docker strace controls to fix the path grammar, reconstructing 1,501 files and 501 directories, then ran the recovered root flag.py (top-down os.walk, reverse-sorted dir and file names, concatenate, SHA-256) to get pokactf2024{<flag redacted — live CTF>}. Sandbox exit 0 and it self-reported exploit_status 'flag-captured', but result.json has flags: [] and meta status is no_flag - the digest was rejected, which is why a retry exists.
